title: Access to finance is not enough: What the International Debt Report 2026 tells us
gist: World Bank International Debt Report 2026 summary: LMIC external debt hit a record $9.4 trillion and debt service rose for a fifth year to $1.4 trillion in 2025 as private lenders and bond markets returned, yet LMICs paid $436.1 billion more than they received in 2022-2025. The poorest (IDA-eligible) countries face borrowing costs not seen since the late 1980s (8.2% on new private lending), so access alone is not enough; transparency and affordable terms matter.

insights.claim: External debt of low- and middle-income countries rose to a record $9.4 trillion, the strongest increase in five years, with even faster growth in IDA-eligible and low-income countries.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Rising leverage in frontier economies increases future restructuring risk.
insights.quote: External debt in LMICs rose to a record $9.4 trillion, marking the strongest increase in five years.

insights.claim: Private lending to LMICs reversed years of decline or stagnation in 2025 as private lenders returned and bond markets reopened.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Frontier Eurobond market reopened; supply of EM paper rising.

insights.claim: Total LMIC debt service rose for a fifth consecutive year in 2025 to $1.4 trillion, with payments to bondholders reaching $363.1 billion.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Bondholders are capturing a growing share of LMIC fiscal resources.
insights.locator: Total debt service for LMICs rose

insights.claim: Between 2022 and 2025 LMICs paid about $436.1 billion more in principal and interest than they received in new financing, a net negative transfer that crowds out investment.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Negative net transfers are a drag on EM growth and a sustainability red flag.
insights.quote: LMICs paid about $436.1 billion more in principal and interest than they received in new financing
insights.locator: Total debt service for LMICs rose

themes.theme: Cost of capital for the poorest

insights.claim: The poorest and most vulnerable countries now face borrowing costs not seen since the late 1980s, with new private lending to IDA-eligible countries averaging 8.2 percent in 2025.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: High coupons attract yield seekers but raise default probability for frontier sovereigns.
insights.quote: New private lending to IDA-eligible countries carry an average of 8.2 percent in 2025.
insights.locator: The poorest countries are paying the most

insights.claim: The gap between what IDA-eligible countries pay private creditors versus official creditors widened from 3.4 percentage points a decade ago to 5.5 percentage points today.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Widening private-official spread shows concessional finance becoming relatively more valuable.
insights.locator: The poorest countries are paying the most

insights.claim: Bond market borrowing by developing countries has continued into 2026 even as yields have risen, raising questions about sustainability of terms.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Issuance at higher yields stores up refinancing risk.
insights.locator: Bond market borrowing has continued into 2026

insights.claim: Borrowing that merely rolls over costly debt is no substitute for financing that expands productive capacity and raises future incomes.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Distinguish refinancing-driven from investment-driven issuance in credit analysis.
insights.locator: Better information must lead to better financing.

insights.claim: During external shocks, countries with heavier debt burdens tend to see larger adverse changes in the share of people who cannot afford a healthy diet.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Debt overhang amplifies social stress and political risk during shocks.
insights.quote: countries with heavier debt burdens tend to see larger adverse changes in the share of people who cannot afford a healthy diet
insights.locator: Debt is not just a financial concern

insights.claim: Over the past decade countries faced a pandemic, supply-chain disruptions, food and energy price spikes, geopolitical fragmentation and repeated financial volatility, which is hardest to absorb with large financing needs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Shock-prone environment raises tail risk for indebted EMs.

insights.claim: Since 2022, creditor data-sharing exercises with the World Bank have reconciled loan-level records, identified discrepancies and closed data gaps in external debt statistics.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Improving data quality may surface previously unrecorded liabilities.
insights.locator: But transparency can't rest on what

insights.claim: New creditors, instruments, guarantees, restructurings and financing arrangements make a country's full obligations harder to see, and without reconciled data creditors cannot assess risk accurately and restructurings get harder.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Opaque collateralized/guaranteed lending complicates restructurings; expect slower workouts.
